state: Locally verified bounded-wait follow-up; no hosted mutation, SQL activation or new native acceptance.

reproduction.eightActualComponentProbes: Both create and reply remained busy after 60,000 virtual milliseconds at digest, getItem, setItem or accepted-receipt cleanup. Preparation had no write and retained the draft; accepted cleanup had one committed row and a cleared draft.

repair: The request-identity preparation phase has one 15,000 ms budget covering hashing, queue wait, getItem and setItem, plus immediate session-cancellation rejection. Every asynchronous boundary and acquired queue rechecks the caller’s dispatch rights.

The deadline retires only the waiting caller. The underlying actual storage operation remains in the per-store/per-key queue until its own promise settles; an expired queued callback cannot later touch storage or dispatch. A pending set is not falsely treated as cancelled.

A current exact-session UI acknowledges a confirmed receipt synchronously as before. It starts ordered UUID cleanup without awaiting it, so local cleanup alone does not hold Send busy. No database receipt or visible draft is guessed.

A later intentional identical request waits behind real cleanup and has its own preparation deadline. After eventual cleanup settlement a deliberate retry creates a different UUID. Different payload keys remain independent and late cleanup preserves newer unsent draft text.
newCoverage: Held digest/get/set each releases busy by the preparation deadline without a write
Late digest/get settlement remains retired; deliberate retry succeeds
Retry started behind a pending set preserves the same saved UUID and commits exactly once
Acknowledged cleanup held in getItem or removeItem never holds Send busy
An identical queued intent can time out without bypassing old cleanup or later dispatching
After actual cleanup settlement a new deliberate identical send commits with a new UUID
A different payload remains independent of another key’s held cleanup
New unsent draft remains after late cleanup
A-to-B-to-A cancels a held hash before it settles, without an intermediate React render
limits: Actual screens/wrappers/shared helper and installed SDK execute in a manual native hook/focus host with controlled Auth/storage/provider and virtual setTimeout. This is not an emulator or native-bridge scheduling proof.
The 32 browser cases use actual React/DOM/pages and synthetic Auth/provider/framework adapters. They preserve existing coverage; no deployed or provider acceptance is claimed.

The 15-second preparation budget is separate from the existing 12-second session lookup and 15-second write/readback deadlines; no single total 15-second latency claim. Confirmation cleanup has no UI wait, but its background storage operation can remain unresolved.

A stalled underlying storage operation intentionally continues to block only its own key. Later attempts fail visibly at their own preparation deadline; the queue is not released early because an uncancellable side effect could otherwise corrupt a newer identity.

Timeout/abort does not establish storage or server rollback. Stable UUID and exact database receipt validation remain required. No automatic write retry, SQL change, new migration invocation, provider write or branch/ref change occurred.
